chunk_findings.detail: The module contract says bad arguments print nothing, but malformed arguments are not rejected. For example, `python -m ddflow.completion_fast ids bug --kind` omits the required `--kind` value; the parser appends `--kind` to `words`, then selects `words[0]` (`"bug"`) as the prefix and can print completions for `"bug"` instead of returning no output. The same issue occurs with extra positional arguments such as `ids alpha beta`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/completion_fast.py:37

chunk_findings.detail: For a record-kind table whose plural is not simple `name + "s"`, the singular canonical kind cannot match it. An index containing `CREATE TABLE memories(id TEXT)` with row `mem-1` and a call `complete_ids('', kind='memory', index=path)` returns `[]`, because `_kind_matches('memory', 'memories')` is False; the function only accepts `name`, `name+"s"`, `name+"es"`, or `name == want+"s"`, and does not handle `y -> ies` (or `-es`) when the table name is already plural. This breaks completion for the listed `memories` kind and for any new `classes`/`categories`-style kind, violating “a new record kind completes automatically”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion_ids.py:_kind_matches

chunk_findings.detail: The lock timeout is 200 ms: `sqlite3.connect(..., timeout=0.2)` (0.2 seconds) and `pragma busy_timeout=200` (200 ms). The stated budget is “sqlite index read in under 100 ms”. In an environment where another ddflow process is writing the index when argcomplete triggers, the read can block for up to 0.2 s before `_guard` catches the lock error and returns no candidates: that is twice the budget and is not reported to the operator.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion_ids.py:_connect

chunk_findings.detail: `CF.complete(["ids", "x"])` is called without changing the process working directory to `tmp_path`. `completion_fast.complete` discovers the index from the current working directory, so if pytest is run from a checkout or worktree that contains a `.ddflow/index.db-*` (e.g., the ddflow repository itself being used to develop this feature), that call finds the real index and returns its IDs. The assertion `CF.complete(["ids", "x"]) == []` then fails even though the isolated `tmp_path/.ddflow` has no index. The test should `monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)` or pass an explicit index.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_ids.py:test_missing_index_gives_nothing

chunk_findings.detail: Malformed arguments are still not rejected for non-`ids` verbs. The parser accepts `--kind`/`--state` unconditionally, even though the CLI contract is `phases|kinds|states [PREFIX]` and says bad arguments print nothing. Input `python -m ddflow.completion_fast phases --kind bug` sets `kind="bug"`, leaves `prefix=""`, and returns `CI.phases("")`, so `main` prints all phases instead of nothing. `kinds --state x` and `states --kind x` do the same for kinds/states. The earlier `ids bug --kind` and extra-positional examples are fixed, but this remaining malformed-argument case still violates the documented contract.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/completion_fast.py:complete

chunk_findings.detail: In `_query_ids`, for a table with a `kind` column, the `kind = ?` filter is only added when `not table_ok`; if the requested kind matches the table name, that filter is skipped. `kinds()` adds every id-bearing table name, including the multi-kind `items`/`records` tables, so a user can ask for `kind='items'` (or singular `kind='item'`, since `_kind_matches('item','items')` is True). Example: index has `CREATE TABLE items(id TEXT, kind TEXT)` with rows `('b-1','bug')` and `('l-1','lesson')`; `complete_ids('', kind='items', index=path)` returns `['b-1','l-1']` even though those rows are `bug` and `lesson` kinds, not `items`. The function should filter by the table’s own `kind` column whenever `kind` is requested and the table has that column.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion_ids.py:_query_ids

chunk_findings.detail: The malformed-argument probes do not actually catch the previously reported bad-argument defect. With the synthetic index, both `CF.complete(["ids", "bug", "--kind"])` and `CF.complete(["ids", "alpha", "beta"])` return `[]` even under the old buggy parser, because the mistaken prefixes `"bug"` and `"alpha"` match no IDs in the fixture (`B1`, `B2`, `COMP-a`, etc.). To guard against finding 1 the test must put a valid prefix before the malformed tail, e.g. `CF.complete(["ids", "COMP", "--kind"]) == []`; the old bug would instead print `COMP-a`/`COMP-b`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_ids.py:test_bad_arguments_print_nothing

chunk_findings.detail: These tests do not enforce the stated 100 ms index-read budget and do not refute previous finding 3. `test_locked_database_gives_nothing_fast` allows up to 2.0 seconds, so the reported 200 ms `busy_timeout` in `_connect` would pass; `test_lookup_latency_budget` allows up to 1.0 second. A locked-index read can block for twice the budget while the suite still reports success. The test should assert the actual budget or verify the operator report rather than only `< 2` / `< 1.0`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_ids.py:test_locked_database_gives_nothing_fast and test_lookup_latency_budget

chunk_findings.detail: When a table has a `kind` column and the requested `kind` fuzzy-matches the table name (for example `kind='item'` matches table `items`), `table_ok` is true, so `_query_ids` never adds the `kind = ?` predicate. The module’s own docstring says `items` and `records` rows carry a `kind` column, so those tables can contain rows of multiple kinds. Given an index DB with `items(id, kind, state)` containing `('bug-1','bug','open')` and `('item-1','item','open')`, `complete_ids('', 'item')` returns both IDs, but should return only `['item-1']`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion_ids.py:_query_ids

chunk_findings.detail: The test is tautological: it explicitly injects `ddflow_slow`, which imports `ddflow.api`, and then only asserts that `ddflow.api` is in `sys.modules`. It never runs the completion budget check or verifies the operator report, so a completion path that imports `ddflow.api` or otherwise violates the under-100 ms budget after the slow import would still leave this test green. It does not test the intent’s falsifier.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_ids.py:test_planted_slow_import_fails_the_budget

chunk_findings.detail: The test calls `CI.complete_ids("x", index=str(tmp_path / "nope"))` and asserts `== []`, but it never asserts that `tmp_path / "nope"` remains absent afterward. Since `sqlite3.connect` on a missing path creates an empty SQLite file by default, a naive `complete_ids` that opens the missing index path mutates the filesystem and still passes this test, violating the stated read-only fallback for missing indexes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_ids.py:test_missing_index_gives_nothing

chunk_findings.detail: `newest_index` selects any directory entry whose name matches `INDEX_NAME` but never checks `e.is_file()`. If `.ddflow` contains a real index file with an older mtime and a directory named, for example, `index.db-ffffffff` with a newer mtime, `newest_index` returns the directory path. `_connect` then tries to open that path with SQLite, raises, and `_guard` swallows the error, so `complete_ids()` returns `[]` even though a valid index file exists. Add a regular-file check before accepting a candidate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion_ids.py:newest_index

chunk_findings.detail: The change still does not answer previous finding 4. Both tests now allow up to 500 ms, which is still 5x the stated 100 ms budget, so an implementation whose `_connect` busy timeout blocks for 200 ms passes: `CI.complete_ids("", index=str(p))` can block for twice the budget and `test_locked_database_gives_nothing_fast` still succeeds because `time.monotonic() - t < 0.5`. `test_lookup_latency_budget` has the same slack, so the suite does not enforce the budget it claims to test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_ids.py:test_locked_database_gives_nothing_fast and test_lookup_latency_budget

chunk_findings.detail: The previous finding still holds: both tests allow up to 500 ms rather than the stated 100 ms budget. `time.monotonic() - t < 0.5` lets an implementation whose `_connect` busy timeout blocks for 200 ms pass, so `test_locked_database_gives_nothing_fast` succeeds even though the TAB could block for twice the budget. `test_lookup_latency_budget` has the same slack, so the suite does not enforce the 100 ms budget it claims to test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_ids.py:test_locked_database_gives_nothing_fast and test_lookup_latency_budget

chunk_findings.detail: The subprocess lookup test still allows `time.monotonic() - t < 0.5`, not the 100 ms budget stated in the change intent. A defective `ddflow.completion_fast` entry point that sleeps 0.4 s before querying the index will pass this test, so the suite still does not enforce the argcomplete-path budget it claims to test. The previous finding is only partly answered: `test_locked_database_gives_nothing_fast` is now tightened to `<0.15`, but this test remains at `<0.5`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_ids.py:test_lookup_latency_budget

chunk_findings.detail: This does not answer the earlier “entry point sleeps” probe. The test now imports `ddflow.completion_fast` and calls `m.complete([...])` directly, so the module’s `if __name__ == "__main__"` block never runs. A `ddflow.completion_fast` whose argcomplete entry point sleeps 0.4 s before calling `complete` will still pass `float(took) < 0.1`, because the measured interval excludes the `__main__` path that `python -m ddflow.completion_fast` actually executes. Thus the suite still does not enforce the actual argcomplete-path budget it was meant to test.
